title: Hand tables (data/<model>_fw<firmware>/hand_tables_<model>_fw<firmware>.json)
description: What the mapping of one model and firmware found by hand about the camera, and the rules the writer applies to its definition: records whose name or note the camera proved wrong, records the menus never write, found by hand, value names no proof can give, the pickers whose lists were walked whole, the values the menus never offer, the copies the camera keeps and the switches that keep a family's copies apart, how far each focus frame can travel, and why a record cannot be proved. Public, and the same for every owner of that model and firmware who maps it: written and edited by hand, never by a kit step. kit/writer/hand_tables.py reads it for kit/schema_update.py, and a camera without the file has every table empty. How, when, in which run and from which state each hand fact was proved is the mapper's evidence: kept in private/evidence/<model>_fw<firmware>.hand.json and put back into the tables as the kit reads them (kit/writer/hand_evidence.py, docs/decisions/0016), so no entry here carries a run, a day, a hand proof's values or the owner's word. Every table is optional. kit/schema_update.py applies them to the camera's definition: the ILCE-1M2 firmware 4.00's own pass reads every table, and every other camera's plain pass reads RECORD_FIXES, FILTER_FLAGS, NEW_RECORDS, NEW_LIKE, NEW_WHOLE_LABELS, FRAME_PROOFS, CAROUSEL, VALUE_FIXES, PP7_VALUES, KEEP_LABELS, PICKER_LISTS, NOT_OFFERED, VIDEO_SYSTEM_VALUES, COPIES, COPY_MODES, COPY_MODES_UNKNOWN, KEEPS_APART, FRAME_TRAVEL, UNPROVED, CONTEXT_WORDS (kit/writer/hand_facts.py) and refuses, in plain words, a file that fills a table it does not read, each marked so below.

$schema.description: This file's JSON Schema, relative to the file.

_comment.description: What the file is, for a person reading it; the kit reads no part of it.

camera.description: The camera the tables are for, <model>_fw<firmware> ("ILCE-1M2_fw4.00"): the kit refuses a file whose camera is not the one its name says.

RECORD_FIXES.description: Records whose name or note the camera proved wrong, by setting key: put on the setting at every write.

FILTER_FLAGS.description: Playback Filter Condition's boxes and their never-set flags, records whose values its options do not name: new records, which NEW_RECORDS takes in by reference.

NEW_RECORDS.description: Records the menus never write, found by hand on the camera, by setting key: added to the definition when it lacks it, laid out from the newest download and like the record `like` names, with the entry's name, values and note (a record a FRAME_PROOFS entry fills keeps its values and note from there). {"$ref": "#/FILTER_FLAGS/<key>"} is FILTER_FLAGS' entry of the same key: one entry in both tables.

NEW_LIKE.description: Records a proof found that the definition lacked, by setting key: laid out like the sibling `like` names (size, count and memory-set presence from the run's start download), named `name`; their values are the proofs' labels, the part after the colon unless NEW_WHOLE_LABELS lists the record.

like.description: The sibling it is laid out like.

NEW_WHOLE_LABELS.description: The NEW_LIKE records whose values take a proof's whole label ("Fluor.: Warm White"), not the part after its colon.

NEW_CHECK_NAMES.description: Names for records first proved through a checklist, by setting key, as their neighbours are named. Read only by the ILCE-1M2's own pass so far: the plain pass, every other camera's, refuses a file that fills it.

LATE_COPY.description: Records the camera writes only once their screen is first saved, by record id ("0x16bd"): the sentence added to the note of a record first proved through a checklist. Read only by the ILCE-1M2's own pass so far: the plain pass, every other camera's, refuses a file that fills it.

ZONE.description: The Zone focus area's grid places, [code, name], as the zone records' values name them; kit/provers/framepos_run.py --zone-grid plans and checks its sweep by them, for the camera the kit works on; no pass of the writer reads it.

FRAME_STEPS.description: How far one press moved a focus frame under each AF Frame Move Amt option, [option, area, x, y]; the notes that give the steps say the same numbers, and the areas they say move alike have the same rows (a test keeps them in step). No pass of the writer reads it: the plain pass, every other camera's, refuses a file that fills it.

FRAME_TRAVEL.description: How far each movable focus frame can travel, by a name for each kind of frame ("Spot", "Custom"): where the camera stops the frame's centre, the records that hold that centre in each place the camera keeps one, and the Focus Area options each limit belongs to, named as the definition's Focus Area values name them. Written as frame on each of those records in the definition (kit/writer/frames.py), only where the hand evidence shows what measured the entry (its "evidence": how it was measured stays private, schemas/hand-evidence.schema.json); an entry that cannot take effect (a record the definition lacks or that names values, a limit outside a record's range, an area no setting of the definition names, a record two entries place differently) is said, "not applied", and left out whole. A place not measured yet (a way of holding the camera not tried) is left out, so its records carry no frame.

FRAME_PROOFS.description: What the mapping found by hand about a record, by setting key: its note, and its values' names where the entry lists them. The hand proof itself (its values, run, day and menu row, a sample's count, the owner's word) is the hand evidence's; an entry that lists values and has no proof there is proved by the report's lines alone.

CAROUSEL.description: Carousel options proved with whatever second-axis value the camera held, [key, value, label]: where the record names only the option, the value takes the option's name. In the plain pass (every camera's but the ILCE-1M2 firmware 4.00's) a value a hand table names is named, not proved: its name counts as checked on the camera (an editor offers it outside Expert mode) only where a proof covers it, the report's or a hand proof with its evidence, or a NOT_OFFERED mark says the camera holds it (held); otherwise its source is "counted". The ILCE-1M2's own pass keeps its meaning until the two passes become one.

VALUE_FIXES.description: Values a proof names with something that is not the value's own (an icon, a carousel's second axis, a word the report took as agreeing), [key, value, label]: the label stands. In the plain pass (every camera's but the ILCE-1M2 firmware 4.00's) a value a hand table names is named, not proved: its name counts as checked on the camera (an editor offers it outside Expert mode) only where a proof covers it, the report's or a hand proof with its evidence, or a NOT_OFFERED mark says the camera holds it (held); otherwise its source is "counted". The ILCE-1M2's own pass keeps its meaning until the two passes become one.

PP7_VALUES.description: Values outside this body's lists that its files hold, [key, value, label]: added to the record's values. In the plain pass (every camera's but the ILCE-1M2 firmware 4.00's) a value a hand table names is named, not proved: its name counts as checked on the camera (an editor offers it outside Expert mode) only where a proof covers it, the report's or a hand proof with its evidence, or a NOT_OFFERED mark says the camera holds it (held); otherwise its source is "counted". The ILCE-1M2's own pass keeps its meaning until the two passes become one.

KEEP_LABELS.description: Records proved by a row whose options do not name their values (a flag several options share, a scale proved by counts): proved, their values keeping the definition's names. In the plain pass a value the definition does not name yet takes the camera's label (no proved value is left without a name), and a name the definition holds stays a hand table's only where the camera read otherwise. In the plain pass (every camera's but the ILCE-1M2 firmware 4.00's) a value a hand table names is named, not proved: its name counts as checked on the camera (an editor offers it outside Expert mode) only where a proof covers it, the report's or a hand proof with its evidence, or a NOT_OFFERED mark says the camera holds it (held); otherwise its source is "counted". The ILCE-1M2's own pass keeps its meaning until the two passes become one.

EV_DOWN_FROM_20.description: Recall Custom holds' Exposure Comp. records whose scale is named by counting quarter stops down from 20, the codes no proof chose "counted". Read only by the ILCE-1M2's own pass so far: the plain pass, every other camera's, refuses a file that fills it.

HOLD_TABLES.description: A Recall Custom hold's copy of a live setting, by the hold's key: named by the live setting's table once that is proved in full and every proof of the hold fits it. Read only by the ILCE-1M2's own pass so far: the plain pass, every other camera's, refuses a file that fills it.

mirror.description: The number the live code is taken from to give the hold's code; null: the code itself.

HOLD_BRACKET_COPIES.description: A hold's bracket record, by its key, and the live bracket setting it copies, numbered by the live code's place in the live list from 0. Read only by the ILCE-1M2's own pass so far: the plain pass, every other camera's, refuses a file that fills it.

ISO_TABLE.description: The record whose values name every ISO Range Limit record's index: the live ISO. Read only by the ILCE-1M2's own pass so far: the plain pass, every other camera's, refuses a file that fills it.

LABEL_FIXES.description: OCR slips the old crawl left in value names, each slip and its mend: applied before anything is compared; a mended name no proof or rule backs stays "schema kept". Read only by the ILCE-1M2's own pass so far: the plain pass, every other camera's, refuses a file that fills it.

GROUP_NAMES.description: The camera's own names for menu groups a breadcrumb was read cut, or with its icon as a letter, each read name and the camera's. Read only by the ILCE-1M2's own pass so far: the plain pass, every other camera's, refuses a file that fills it.

MY_MENU_ROW.description: The menu row whose proofs add My Menu's items: the writer reads those proofs, not the report's row. Read only by the ILCE-1M2's own pass so far: the plain pass, every other camera's, refuses a file that fills it.

MY_MENU_EMPTY.description: My Menu's empty place, named in every slot. Read only by the ILCE-1M2's own pass so far: the plain pass, every other camera's, refuses a file that fills it.

line.description: The line added to each slot's note; {code} is the camera file's my_menu.empty.

SHOOT_MODE_RECORDS.description: By shooting family, the records whose values that family's Shoot Mode carousel describes. Read only by the ILCE-1M2's own pass so far: the plain pass, every other camera's, refuses a file that fills it.

PICKER_LISTS.description: Pickers whose lists were walked whole on the camera, by a name for each (the picker, or the key whose walk proves the list): each setting an entry covers lists exactly the codes its picker's walks wrote, and a value a first kit listed beyond them (from a union of the camera's function codes) is taken out (kit/writer/offered.py walked_lists), before the not-offered marks. Only while the walks and the table walk show the list whole and one for every setting covered (each through a row of its own), every row of a covered setting was made in a state a walk names, the hand evidence says how it was walked, and no proof, not the definition's sample and none of the camera's own downloads holds a code outside it; otherwise the lists stay as they are, said, or the write stops. For a picker whose list does not change with the camera's state: where it may, walk it in each state, every walk named, or mark its values NOT_OFFERED. Where a value is on another key's list of the same picker screen, or the camera writes it itself, a NOT_OFFERED mark says so instead.

NOT_OFFERED.description: Values the camera's menus never offer, each mark written only while its evidence holds (kit/writer/offered.py); the order is the writer's.

VIDEO_SYSTEM_VALUES.description: Values offered under one video system only, by setting key, where no proof walked the row under each system: both keys always, the other's empty when every value listed is one system's.

COPIES.description: The values the camera keeps in more than one record, by the live setting's key: its Stills copy and its Movie copy, in that order. A memory set's own record ("set:...") the camera writes alike in others (the a1 II's Zone place for each way of holding the camera) is a family too, its copies' modes not known (COPY_MODES_UNKNOWN), checked in every memory set of the camera's downloads.

COPY_MODES.description: The modes whose value each copy is, by its place in COPIES, named as camera.memory_sets.modes names them.

COPY_MODES_UNKNOWN.description: The COPIES families whose copies' modes are not known yet: they carry no copy_for, and the write checks the weaker rule.

KEEPS_APART.description: The camera's own switches that keep a COPIES family's per-mode copies apart (the a1 II's Different Set for Still/Mv boxes), by the switch's key: what each keeps apart, where a proof on the camera showed what the switch does to the family's copies, and only there (a switch whose effect is not proved gets no entry). Written as keeps_apart on the switch's setting in the definition (kit/writer/copies.py) where the definition holds the family with its copies and their modes, the hand evidence shows the entry (its "evidence", and its "untick" for untick_sets: what proved it stays private, schemas/hand-evidence.schema.json), and no download of the camera's holds the switch outside apart with the family at more than one value (one that does stops the write); an entry that cannot take effect is said, "not applied", and left out.

UNPROVED.description: Why no proof can reach a record, by setting key: [kind, null, why], the kind one the definition's unproved_reason lists and the why in a photographer's words; the day it was settled is the hand evidence's (null here).

CONTEXT_WORDS.description: Proof contexts in other words, a pattern (Python's) and its words, applied in this order where a row enters the definition and to the rows it kept.

ORIENTED.description: A pattern (Python's) for the report's rows proved holding the camera one way; its group names the way. Read only by the ILCE-1M2's own pass so far: the plain pass, every other camera's, refuses a file that fills it.

key.description: A setting's key, as the definition keys it.

note.description: Its note (a note's evidence is the hand evidence's).

like.description: The record whose tab, group, order and modes it takes.

values.description: Its values' names, a hand table's. In the plain pass (every camera's but the ILCE-1M2 firmware 4.00's) a value a hand table names is named, not proved: its name counts as checked on the camera (an editor offers it outside Expert mode) only where a proof covers it, the report's or a hand proof with its evidence, or a NOT_OFFERED mark says the camera holds it (held); otherwise its source is "counted". The ILCE-1M2's own pass keeps its meaning until the two passes become one.

note.description: Its note (empty where a FRAME_PROOFS entry gives it).

$ref.description: FILTER_FLAGS' entry of the same key.

note.description: What the record holds, in plain words.

values.description: Its values' names, a hand table's. In the plain pass (every camera's but the ILCE-1M2 firmware 4.00's) a value a hand table names is named, not proved: its name counts as checked on the camera (an editor offers it outside Expert mode) only where a proof covers it, the report's or a hand proof with its evidence, or a NOT_OFFERED mark says the camera holds it (held); otherwise its source is "counted". The ILCE-1M2's own pass keeps its meaning until the two passes become one.

keys.description: A pattern (Python's) for the keys of the settings the list is for: an array record's slots, or keys whose pickers offer one list ("^global:0x0445\\[(?:[0-9]|1[01])\\]$").

walk.description: A pattern (Python's) for the report's rows that walked the list whole, one in each state the list was proved in: each proves one setting it covers, chose every place by its proof lines (no sample from the option the camera held) and names as many options and wrote as many distinct codes as the list has places, all of them the same codes. A row may walk another slot or key than the setting's own: the table walk shows every setting's picker lists the same functions in the same order.

table.description: The table walk's screen the pickers are on, [screen, page or section or null]: a keyset's page by its title, a table's section by the start of its rows' labels ("Still" for the Fn menu's Still Upper and Still Lower), null for the whole screen. Each setting's picker is found there through a report row that proves the setting, and every one went round to its start.

why.description: Why the list is the picker's whole list, in plain words (that it was walked full circle, and whose codes the others are), naming no run and no day.

values.description: The values the menus never offer.

why.description: Why, in plain words, for the editor (it says them after "Not on the camera's list: A, B."), naming neither the values nor how many.

menu.description: The menu whose list leaves them out.

walk.description: A pattern (Python's) for the report's rows that walked the row's whole list: each must prove the record and none may write the value; a row that chose only a sample of a picker from the option the camera held counts for none. Where no row it names proves the record, a row it names that walked another key's or slot's picker whole stands for it when the table walk shows both pickers listing the same functions in the same order.

table.description: The table walk's screen, [table, page or null], every picker list of which must go round to its start without the function.

held.description: A value the camera writes itself (its factory value) and the list cannot choose back: an editor keeps offering it.

named_by.description: The record whose proved names name a held value.

setting.description: The family's setting: a COPIES family whose copies' modes the table names (not one of COPY_MODES_UNKNOWN).

apart.description: The switch's values with which the camera keeps the family's copies apart (the box's Ticked); with any other the copies share one value. Each one of the switch's values, never all of them.

untick_sets.description: What the camera set the family's setting and each of its copies to when the switch was changed from a value in apart to one that is not (the box unticked), in the states the proof tried: one of the setting's values and each copy's. Absent where that was not proved; written only where the hand evidence shows it (its "untick").

places.description: A frame measured area by area: the [X, Y] record pairs that hold its centre, a pair for each place the camera keeps it in (in use, level, a grip's copy).

limits.description: With places: where the frame's centre stops, by area, each Focus Area option in one entry at most (areas whose limits are the same share one).

by.description: The setting whose value, read in the same section as the place, picks the limits (the a1 II's Aspect Ratio, where the limits change): with it every limit says the values it is for (when), and boxes give each value's picture (pictures). Left out where the limits hold whatever the camera's settings.

in_modes.description: How each shooting mode's sections pick the limits, where the mode decides: each entry's modes read by, or take the limits for one value of it (as), inferred or measured. A section of a mode no entry names has no limits known (the a1 II's Time-lapse sets, and its Custom boxes' own places outside Stills). Absent: every section reads by. Each mode in one entry at most; a box may give its own (frame_box), for its places alone.

inside.description: Boxes whose size the file holds: the camera keeps the whole box, centred on its place, inside these bounds on the grid's whole span (fractions allowed, as the rule that reproduces every measured limit needs them), so its centre stops half the box's width (height) inside them, each end rounded to the nearest whole number, a half toward the centre.

sizes_tried.description: With inside and no pictures: the widths (x) and heights (y) the boxes stood at when the rule was proved; at any other size it is not tried. Left out where that is not known; with pictures each picture holds its own.

grid.description: With pictures: the span of the grid the positions are on, {"x": 640, "y": 480} for the a1 II; its centre is half of it.

pictures.description: With by: for each of its values, the part of the grid's span the recorded picture covers on each axis, centred. The grid is stretched over the picture, while inside and the boxes' sizes stay measured on the whole span; so a box's centre stays where the whole box is inside both inside and the picture, mapped onto the stretched grid, each end rounded to the nearest whole number, a half toward the centre. Each value in one picture at most.

boxes.description: With inside: each box the rule holds for, a box in use whichever it is among them.

frame_travel.description: One kind of focus frame, in one of two shapes: a frame whose limits were measured area by area (places and limits: the a1 II's spot sizes and Expand Spot, whose size no record holds), or boxes whose size the file holds, which one rule bounds (inside, boxes and, where known, sizes_tried: the a1 II's Custom boxes). Where the limits change with a setting of the camera's (by), each limit or picture names the values it is for. A position is the frame's centre on the camera's grid (the a1 II's 640 x 480), as its records hold it; a press that would take the frame past a limit stops it there.

frame_pair.description: [the X record, the Y record] (for a box's size: [its width's, its height's]), two records.

frame_bounds.description: {"x": [left, right], "y": [top, bottom]} on the camera's grid.

frame_sizes.description: Sizes, as the size records hold them.

frame_areas.description: Focus Area options, each named as a setting of the definition names it among its values ("Spot: M", "Tracking: Spot M").

areas.description: The areas these limits are for.

x.description: The X the centre stops at, [left, right].

y.description: The Y the centre stops at, [top, bottom].

when.description: With its entry's by: the values of that setting these limits are for.

frame_limit.description: Where a measured frame's centre stops, for some areas.

areas.description: The areas that use the box.

size.description: The records that hold the box's size, [width, height], in each section the places are read in.

places.description: The [X, Y] record pairs that hold the box's centre, a pair for each place the camera keeps it in.

in_modes.description: This box's own in_modes, for its places alone, in place of its entry's (the a1 II's box in use, whose size records hold the size the rule reads in Movie too).

frame_box.description: A box the rule bounds: its areas, its size records and the records of its places.

when.description: The values of the entry's by this picture is for.

x.description: The part of the grid's width the picture covers.

y.description: The part of the grid's height the picture covers.

sizes_tried.description: The widths (x) and heights (y) the boxes stood at when the rule was proved for these values; at any other size it is not tried.

sizes_range.description: The widths (x) and heights (y) the sizes the rule was proved across, [smallest, largest]: tried at both and at sizes between, every one giving the measured limits exactly, the rule's form the same at every size, so every size in it counts as tried (as samples on a line establish a scale); in place of sizes_tried.

frame_picture.description: The picture for some values of the entry's by.

frame_fraction.description: [numerator, denominator], the numerator not above the denominator.

modes.description: Shooting modes, as camera.memory_sets.modes names them ("Stills", "Movie", "S&Q", "Time-lapse"); a memory set's mode is the one it is listed under, the live settings' camera.live_mode's.

as.description: The value of by whose limits hold in these modes, by not read there (the a1 II's Movie: Stills' at 16:9, whatever Aspect Ratio holds). Without it these modes read by.

inferred.description: With as: that was inferred, not measured, in these modes (the a1 II's S&Q, taken as Movie): an editor says so where it places a frame by it.

frame_mode.description: How the sections of some shooting modes pick the frame's limits.
